newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX ends at new high of 7,412.71pts.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX ends at new high of 7,412.71pts.

text.p: Hungarian share prices powered ahead on Tuesday, driving the BUX index to a new high as fresh capital reached the market partly at the expense of the Czech and Polish markets, traders and analysts said.

"Floods in Poland and the Czech Republic may have a very serious macroeconomic impact in those countries -- obviously the floods have a direct impact on their bourses as well," one trader said, adding certain money left these markets for the Hungarian.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary new high of 7,412.71 points, up 142.77 points or 1.96 percent.
BUX futures also traded firmer with September adding 159.5 points to finish at 7,660 and the most actively traded December maturity firming 159.5 points to end at 8,099.

"(Pharmaceuticals) Richter and OTP Bank rallied even though they have not been cheap so far," the trader said. "But apparently investing in Hungary is more important than the price of the share itself."
The dollar's strength contributed to the market's rise by making the forint, thus Hungarian shares, cheaper for foreign investors who pay for the papers with U.S. currency, they said.
At midday's close the forint traded at 192.02/07 to the dollar, compared to 191.25/30 at opening.
"A strong dollar makes Hungarian shares cheaper for those investors who invest in Hungary," the trader said.

Foreign investors on the Budapest Stock Exchange are dominated by UK- and US-based funds, but market participants said on Tuesday they played a smaller role, giving the lead to domestic investors and late-arriving west Europeans.

Other market participants said earlier today that comments by the Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker that Hungary has made "impressive progress" towards European Union membership could have a beneficial impact on the bourse.
An analyst also said the Hungarian market capitalised on the serious flood problems in Poland and the Czech Republic, but added he expected the market still to head downwards this week.

"I expect the market to turn lower this week as the... market is far from being cheap (although) this does not mean that certain stocks would not be attractive," said Robert Feuer, analyst at WestMerchant in London, adding he saw the market's growth potentials limited.
OTP finished at a new high of 6,290 forints, up 245, while Richter at 17,895 forints, up 395.
Retailer Fotex strengthened to 222 forints, up 22. Its biggest single shareholder, the Panama-registered Blackburn International said it bought 20,000 Fotex shares on July 11.
This was Blackburn's sixth announcement this month that it had bought Fotex shares. Each purchase was between 10,000 and 27,000 units.
Elsewhere, the chemicals stocks were firmer as TVK surged to a new high of 3,945 forints before retreating to close at 3,940, up 130. BorsodChem added 50 forints to finish at 7,600.
Feuer said that the market expected good first-half results for TVK as world market prices favour the company, but warned the world chemical cycle might turn for the worse next year.
"Valuation of a chemical company should also reflect the cyclical nature of the industy, therefore I don't think TVK could substantially improve in terms of price/earnings ratio."
